name: Build-a-Cycle Moon
instructions: Tap a petal, then tap its place on the moon. Start at the top right and go round.

slots.label: Period
slots.fact: The cosy lining gently leaves the body. That’s your period!
slots.hint: The cycle starts with the period, at the top right.

slots.label: Egg growing
slots.fact: A new egg grows inside the ovary, and a fresh lining starts to build.
slots.hint: After the period, something starts to grow.

slots.label: Egg released
slots.fact: The ovary releases the egg. This is called ovulation.
slots.hint: Halfway round, the egg is let go.

slots.label: Lining waiting
slots.fact: The lining waits. If it isn’t needed, the cycle begins again.
slots.hint: Last comes the waiting part, before it all starts again.

config.footnote: Days shown for a 28-day cycle. Every body has its own rhythm.
config.done_line: The moon turns once for every cycle, just like your body.

config.instructions: Every girl travels through puberty in her own order. Tap each stop, read what happens, and stamp your passport.
config.done_line: 8 of 8 stamps. Remember: everyone visits these stops in her own order and her own time.

cards.name: Breast buds
cards.back: Small, tender bumps under the nipples are often the first sign. One side may grow first, that’s okay.
cards.tip: A soft cotton slip or starter bra can feel comfy.

cards.name: Body hair
cards.back: Hair grows under the arms, on the legs and around the private parts.
cards.tip: Removing it is your choice, never a must.

cards.name: Growth spurt
cards.back: You may grow several centimetres in a year. Clothes suddenly feel short!
cards.tip: Good sleep and food help growing bones.

cards.name: New shape
cards.back: Hips widen and the body gets softer curves. Every shape is a healthy shape.

cards.name: Skin and sweat
cards.back: Oil and sweat glands wake up, so pimples and body odour can appear.
cards.tip: Wash your face twice a day and bathe daily.

cards.name: First period
cards.back: Menarche usually comes about 2 years after breast buds start, often between 9 and 15.
cards.tip: Keep a pad in your bag once breast buds appear.

cards.name: Big feelings
cards.back: Oestrogen and progesterone can make feelings go up and down quickly.
cards.tip: Name the feeling, then breathe or talk.

cards.name: Irregular at first
cards.back: Periods can be far apart or close together for the first 1 to 2 years.
cards.tip: Track it in your Diary to spot your rhythm.

config.instructions: Six case files have landed on your desk. Read each clue and crack the case.
config.done_line: You read the clues like a pro. Flow changes, stress can shift it, and heavy or long periods mean tell a grown-up.

cases.scene: Sana sees just a few brownish spots on her pad.
cases.question: What kind of flow is this?
cases.feedback: Light flow. Brown blood is simply older blood, totally normal at the start or end.

cases.scene: Mira changes a well-used pad every 4 to 5 hours.
cases.question: What kind of flow is this?
cases.feedback: Medium flow, and she’s changing on time. Case closed!

cases.scene: Tara soaks through a pad every hour for several hours and feels dizzy.
cases.question: What should Tara do?

options.text: Tell a grown-up and see a doctor

cases.feedback: Very heavy flow with dizziness needs a doctor. Telling a grown-up is the brave, smart move.

cases.scene: Anu’s period came 10 days late during board-exam week.
cases.question: What’s the likely clue?
cases.feedback: Stress can shift the cycle. If it keeps happening, she can check with a doctor.

cases.scene: Ira’s period has now lasted 9 days.
cases.question: What should Ira do?

options.text: Tell a grown-up: more than 7 days is worth checking

cases.feedback: Periods usually last 2 to 7 days. Longer is a good reason to see a doctor.

cases.scene: Neha’s aunt says she must not bathe during her period.
cases.question: Myth or fact?
cases.feedback: Myth busted! A warm bath keeps you fresh and can ease cramps.

config.instructions: Build your care clock! Tap the right time for each habit, and catch the ones to skip.
config.done_line: Daily freshness, on-time changes, a night pad, and no perfumes. That’s a Care Captain routine.

items.text: Bath, and wash outside with plain water
items.explanation: A daily bath keeps you fresh. Water outside is all you need.

items.text: Put on fresh cotton underwear
items.explanation: Cotton lets skin breathe, so germs don’t grow.

items.text: Change my pad (every 4 to 6 hours)
items.explanation: On-time changes stop smell, rashes and germs.

items.text: Wash my hands before and after
items.explanation: Clean hands, clean change.

items.text: Wipe from front to back
items.explanation: Every time you use the toilet, too.

items.text: Wear a fresh, longer pad for the night
items.explanation: Night pads are longer, so you can sleep without worry.

items.text: Spray perfume down there
items.explanation: Scents irritate delicate skin. Skip it!

items.text: Wash inside the vagina with soap
items.explanation: The vagina cleans itself. Soap inside upsets its balance.

items.text: Wear the same pad all day
items.explanation: Germs grow in a used pad. Change every 4 to 6 hours.

config.instructions: Four friends need help choosing a period product. Read about each one and make the match.
config.done_line: Every product has pros and cons. The best one is the one that suits your body, your day and your planet.

cases.scene: Zoya expects her first period soon and wants something simple to start with.
cases.question: What would you suggest?
cases.feedback: Pads are easy and a great first choice. Pros: simple, many sizes. Cons: single use, so more waste.

cases.scene: Diya swims for her school team and has a meet during her period.
cases.question: What could work in the pool?
cases.feedback: Pads don’t work in water. Tampons or cups can, once she’s comfortable and has asked a grown-up.

cases.scene: Meher loves the planet and wants less waste.
cases.question: Which match fits Meher?
cases.feedback: One cup can last years. Pros: less waste, saves money. Cons: needs practice and washing.

cases.scene: Kiara has a 2-hour bus ride on a heavy-flow day.
cases.question: What should she pack?

options.text: A long heavy-flow pad, plus a spare

cases.feedback: Heavy days need higher absorbency, and a spare in the pouch means no worries.

config.instructions: Tap the steps in the right order. Two rounds: changing a pad, then caring for a cloth pad.
config.done_line: Clean hands, wrap and bin, never flush, and sunshine for cloth pads.

rounds.name: Change a pad
steps_in_order: Roll it up in the wrapper or paper
Stick the new pad in place

rounds.name: Care for a cloth pad
steps_in_order: Fold and keep in a clean pouch

config.wrong_hint: Not yet! Think about what has to happen before that.

name: School Day Surprise
instructions: A branching story, then pack your own school pouch.

nodes.text: Maths class, second period. Aanya feels something different… she thinks her period has started!

choices.label: Raise her hand to use the washroom

nodes.text: Zoya smiles: "Happens to all of us! Let’s tell Ms. Kapoor together."
The bell is still 30 minutes away. Aanya feels a bit worried.
nodes.gigi: Your body is never a disturbance. It’s always okay to step out.

nodes.text: Ms. Kapoor nods kindly and lets her go. No questions, no fuss.
"May I use the washroom, please?" The teacher says yes with a smile.
In the washroom, Aanya takes a deep breath. She’s got this.

choices.label: The emergency pouch in her bag

nodes.text: Fresh pad, wrap the used one, bin it, wash hands. Back in class in 5 minutes, feeling proud!
The nurse has pads ready and a kind smile. Next time, a pouch in her bag will make it even easier.

pack.wrong_msg: That one can stay at home.

with_flag.title: Kit Packer badge!
with_flag.line: You planned ahead and handled it like a pro.

without_flag.title: Story complete!
without_flag.line: Asking for help is brave. Try the story again to find the bonus badge!

config.instructions: Gigi’s body map is glowing in 4 places. Tap a spot, then pick the comfort tools that help.
config.done_line: Warmth, movement, water and rest. You know what helps your body feel better.

spots.name: Tummy cramps
spots.tip: Warmth relaxes the squeezing muscles, and gentle movement helps too.

spots.name: Lower back ache
spots.tip: A warm bottle on the back and a cat-cow stretch can ease it.

spots.name: Bloated belly
spots.tip: Water and less salt help your body let go of extra water.

spots.name: Feeling tired
spots.tip: Rest, water and a little fresh air can recharge you.

config.warning: Tell a grown-up if pain stops you from going to school, or if it doesn’t get better. Medicine only with a parent or doctor.

config.instructions: Sort each clue. Is it usually normal, or a sign to tell a grown-up and see a doctor?
config.done_line: You can spot what’s usually normal and what needs a doctor. And remember: you can tell a grown-up about anything.

items.text: Mild cramps on day 1 or 2
items.explanation: Common, and warmth or a stretch helps.

items.text: Cycles of 25 to 40 days in the first year
items.explanation: Normal while your body settles.

items.text: Feeling a bit tired during your period
items.explanation: Common. Rest and water help.

items.text: Pain so strong you miss school every month
items.explanation: This could be endometriosis or something else a doctor can treat.

items.text: Soaking a pad every 1 to 2 hours
items.explanation: That’s menorrhagia, very heavy bleeding. A doctor can help.

items.text: No period by age 15
items.explanation: That’s called primary amenorrhea. A check-up gives answers.

items.text: Periods stop for 3 months after being regular
items.explanation: Worth checking, even if you feel fine.

items.text: Very irregular periods with lots of acne or extra hair
items.explanation: These can be signs of PCOS, which a doctor can manage.

config.instructions: Germs are knocking! Decide which habits shield you and which ones let germs in.
config.done_line: Cotton, on-time changes, front to back and dry skin. And if something itches or smells strange, you tell.

items.text: Cotton underwear
items.explanation: Cotton breathes, so germs can’t settle in.

items.text: Changing pads every 4 to 6 hours
items.explanation: Fresh pads, fewer germs.

items.text: Wiping front to back
items.explanation: Keeps germs from the back passage away.

items.text: Drying well after a bath
items.explanation: Germs love damp places.

items.text: Telling a grown-up about itching
items.explanation: The fastest way to get treated.

items.text: Scented sprays and washes
items.explanation: They upset the good bacteria.

items.text: Sitting in a wet swimsuit for hours
items.explanation: Damp, tight clothes help yeast grow. Change soon after swimming.

items.text: Washing inside the vagina (douching)
items.explanation: It washes away the good bacteria that protect you.

config.instructions: Four moments at school and online. What would an upstander do?
config.done_line: You don’t join in, you include, and you tell. That’s how safe schools are built.

cases.scene: Someone posts a meme making fun of Riya’s teeth. Everyone is sending laughing faces.
cases.question: What would an upstander do?

options.text: Don’t share it, send Riya something kind, tell a teacher

cases.feedback: Not sharing stops it spreading. A kind message and an adult’s help make a big difference.

cases.scene: A group won’t let Ananya sit with them, again and again.
cases.question: What could you do?

options.text: Invite Ananya to sit with you

cases.feedback: Including someone is a quiet, powerful way to stand up.

cases.scene: Someone keeps calling you names and it really hurts.
cases.question: What’s a good step?
cases.feedback: It’s not your fault. Telling isn’t tattling, it’s getting help.

cases.scene: A stranger in a game chat asks for your photo and your school name.
cases.question: What should you do?

options.text: Don’t reply, block, and tell a grown-up

cases.feedback: Never share photos or personal details with strangers online. Block and tell.

config.instructions: Sort each moment calmly. Take your time, there’s no timer here.
config.done_line: Safe touch is never secret. You can say no, and you can always tell.

items.text: A high five from a friend
items.explanation: A friendly touch you’re happy with is safe.

items.text: A hug from Nani that you like
items.explanation: Safe touch feels good and is never secret.

items.text: A doctor’s check-up with Mom in the room
items.explanation: A doctor may need to check you, with a parent there.

items.text: A hug from a relative that you don’t want
items.explanation: You can say, “I’d like a high five instead.” Your body, your choice.

items.text: A friend keeps tickling after you said stop
items.explanation: Stop means stop. Say no firmly, and tell an adult if it continues.

items.text: Someone touches the parts a swimsuit covers
items.explanation: Say NO, GO away, and TELL a trusted adult. It’s never your fault.

items.text: An adult says, “This touch is our little secret”
items.explanation: Touch should never be a secret. Tell someone you trust.

items.text: Someone shows you pictures that make you uncomfortable
items.explanation: That’s not okay. Leave and tell a trusted adult.

outro_steps: TELL a trusted adult, and keep telling

config.instructions: Collect your 6 rights cards. Tap each one to learn what the law promises you.
config.done_line: The law is on your side. You are protected, you will be believed, and help is one call away.

cards.name: Protected till 18
cards.back: POCSO protects every child in India under 18 years.
cards.tip: That includes you, and your friends.

cards.name: Every child
cards.back: Girls, boys, every child is protected the same way.

cards.name: Never your fault
cards.back: Under 18, the law says a child cannot agree to sexual acts. The adult is always responsible.
cards.tip: Even if someone says “you said yes”.

cards.name: Name kept private
cards.back: A child’s name, photo or school can’t be shared in the news.

cards.name: Child-friendly help
cards.back: Special courts and trained officers make it easier to speak. A trusted adult can stay with you.

cards.name: Anyone can report
cards.back: A child, parent, teacher or neighbour can call 1098 or 112, or go to the police.

config.instructions: Is it a green flag (healthy) or a red flag (not okay) in a friendship? Wave the right flag!
config.done_line: Keep the green flags close. For red flags, use your “I feel… when… I need…” words, and talk to a trusted adult.

items.text: Celebrates when you do well
items.explanation: Real friends cheer for you.

items.text: Says sorry after hurting you
items.explanation: Owning mistakes builds trust.

items.text: Respects it when you say no
items.explanation: A no should be accepted, every time.

items.text: Listens when you talk
items.explanation: Feeling heard is a sign of a good friendship.

items.text: Makes fun of you in front of others
items.explanation: Jokes that hurt aren’t jokes.

items.text: Pressures you to do things you don’t want
items.explanation: Good friends never push you.

items.text: Gets angry when you have other friends
items.explanation: You can have many friends.

items.text: Shares your private chats
items.explanation: Breaking trust is a red flag.

outro_steps: I need… (ask for what would help)

name: Mood Garden
instructions: Pick a mood flower, choose a coping tool, then breathe with the flower.

moods.label: Happy
moods.line: Yay! Happy feelings are worth noticing too.
tools: Share it with someone you love

moods.label: Calm
moods.line: Calm is a lovely place to be.
tools: Enjoy the quiet for a minute

moods.label: Tired
tools: Go to bed a little earlier

moods.label: Crampy
moods.line: Cramps are no fun. Let’s be gentle.
tools: Tell a grown-up if it hurts a lot

moods.label: Worried
moods.line: Worries feel big. You don’t have to carry them alone.
tools: Talk to someone in your Safe Circle
Put it in your Worry Jar

moods.label: Grumpy
moods.line: Grumpy happens to everyone. It will pass.
tools: Say what’s bugging you out loud
